title: Theory of Computation Fill in the Blanks Quiz
description: Fill in the blanks practice questions covering Finite Automata, CFGs, Turing Machines, and Complexity Classes.
heading: Theory of Computation Fill in the Blanks

questions.question: A finite non-empty set of symbols is called an ____________.
questions.hint: It is denoted by Sigma (Σ).

questions.question: A sequence of symbols from an alphabet is called a ____________.
questions.hint: It is a finite sequence, also sometimes called a word.

questions.question: Chomsky classification divides languages into ____________ types.
questions.hint: Classes range from Type-0 to Type-3.

questions.question: A deterministic finite automaton has exactly ____________ transition for each input symbol.
questions.hint: There is no choice or ambiguity for the next state transition.

questions.question: The process of reducing states in a DFA without changing its language is called ____________.
questions.hint: It creates an equivalent automaton with the smallest possible number of states.

questions.question: A grammar that generates context-free languages is called ____________.
questions.hint: Its production rules are of the form A → α, where A is a single non-terminal.

questions.question: The tree that shows derivation of a string is called a ____________.
questions.hint: A graphical representation of the sequential substitution steps.

questions.question: A grammar is ____________ if a string has more than one parse tree.
questions.hint: It provides multiple distinct structural meanings for the same input string.

questions.question: A pushdown automaton uses a ____________ as memory structure.
questions.hint: A Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) storage structure.

questions.question: Chomsky Normal Form allows productions of type A → BC or A → ____________.
questions.hint: The right-hand side can only be exactly two variables or a single unit symbol.

questions.question: A Turing Machine consists of an infinite ____________.
questions.hint: An unbounded storage medium divided into sequential cells.

questions.question: The Church-Turing thesis relates to ____________.
questions.hint: It defines what can effectively be calculated by any mechanical device.

questions.question: Languages accepted by Turing Machines are called ____________ languages.
questions.hint: Also known as Type-0 or semi-decidable languages.

questions.question: The problem of deciding whether a program halts is called ____________ problem.
questions.hint: Alan Turing proved that this specific problem has no general algorithmic solution.

questions.question: A problem for which no algorithm exists is called ____________.
questions.hint: It is impossible to construct a correct yes/no answer for every input instance.

questions.question: Class P consists of problems solvable in ____________ time.
questions.hint: Considered the baseline class for computationally tractable problems.

questions.question: NP stands for ____________ Polynomial time.
questions.hint: Refers to the behavior of the abstract machine executing parallel choice routes.

questions.question: Problems whose solutions can be verified quickly belong to class ____________.
questions.hint: A deterministic machine can verify a given solution certificate in polynomial time.

questions.question: Co-NP is the class of complements of problems in ____________.
questions.hint: Includes problems whose 'no' instances can be verified in polynomial time.

questions.question: Time complexity measures the amount of ____________ required by an algorithm.
questions.hint: Quantifies steps or runtime relative to the operational scale of input size.

questions.question: Cook’s Theorem shows that SAT is ____________-complete.
questions.hint: It was the first problem proven to be the hardest in class NP.

questions.question: PSPACE refers to problems solvable using polynomial ____________.
questions.hint: Focuses on runtime memory constraints rather than execution step limits.

questions.question: Savitch’s Theorem relates NSPACE with ____________ space.
questions.hint: Shows that non-deterministic space can be simulated deterministically with a squaring factor.

questions.question: The class L refers to problems solvable in ____________ space.
questions.hint: Deterministic memory proportional to log(n).

questions.question: NL is the class of problems solvable using ____________ logarithmic space.
questions.hint: Corresponds to space scaling bounds using non-deterministic decision routes.
